title: Sonja Henie's birth chart
metaDescription: Sonja Henie's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.2° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 18.2° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 18.2° Aries. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 29.2° Aries; Venus stands at 24.9° Pisces; Mars stands at 1.6° Cancer. The tradition reads a mind that decides at speaking speed from Mercury, taste tuned to mood and undertow from Venus, drive that moves on certainty and current from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Saturn and Neptune: 2.0° from an exact sextile. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Mercury sextile Pluto at 2.1°, and Venus square Pluto at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 18.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 24.9° is in exaltation; Mars in Cancer at 1.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 15.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 fire, 3 water, 2 air, 1 earth by element and 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. Fire leads with ignition: the first move made early, and certainty arriving ahead of the evidence. Mercury and Jupiter were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
